units.summary: The test now builds its breaker with the two-step constructor to match the new groupBreaker type. Assertions are unchanged, so a line-by-line review can be skipped.
units.headline: Reconcile-preserves-state test uses two-step breaker constructor
units.reason: Test-only type adaptation to the new breaker type; no assertions removed or changed.

units.summary: The test now builds the old breaker with the two-step constructor to match the new groupBreaker type. Assertions are unchanged, so a line-by-line review can be skipped.
units.headline: Changed-key reset test uses two-step breaker constructor
units.reason: Test-only type adaptation to the new breaker type; no assertions removed or changed.

units.summary: handlerEntry now holds the two-step breaker plus a per-handler watches context and its cancel func. reconcile cancels it when the handler is replaced or removed, so streaming watches end and clients re-watch.
units.headline: handlerEntry gains two-step breaker and per-handler watch context
units.reason: Adds struct fields and a cancellation lifecycle that changes how long-lived watch requests end.
focus: Places that build handlerEntry directly (tests omit watches/endWatches) tolerate nil watches
Every discarded entry is cancelled, so no context leaks

units.summary: New constructor creates a handlerEntry with a fresh breaker and a cancellable watches context. It replaces the inline struct literal and in-place mutation in reconcile.
units.headline: New newHandlerEntry constructor creates breaker and watch context together
units.reason: Creates cancellable contexts whose lifecycle governs when in-flight watches are terminated.
focus: endWatches is called on every path where an entry is discarded
Deriving the context from Background rather than the service context is intended

units.summary: servingEntry now carries the groupBreaker type and the handler's watches context so the request path can scope watches to the handler generation.
units.headline: servingEntry carries watch context and groupBreaker type
units.reason: Struct field change on the request-serving snapshot that drives watch termination.
focus: Snapshot entries with nil watches are handled by serveWatch

units.summary: The router creates a root watches context at construction, to be cancelled by closeWatches at service stop.
units.headline: Router creates a root context for ending all watches
units.reason: Adds lifecycle context affecting shutdown behavior of long-running requests.
focus: closeWatches cancels this context, and routers built elsewhere are not left with a nil one

units.summary: A changed key now replaces the handlerEntry instead of mutating it, and replaced or removed entries have their watches cancelled after publish. Clients with open watches are disconnected on backend changes and must re-watch.
units.headline: Reconcile replaces changed entries and ends their watches after publish
units.reason: Changes handler replacement semantics and terminates live client connections on backend change.
focus: Cancellation after publish lets re-watching clients reach the new backend
Early returns before the cancel loop do not leak retired entries
Breaker reset for changed keys and preservation for unchanged keys still hold

units.summary: The published snapshot entry now includes the handler's watches context so requests can bind watches to the current handler generation.
units.headline: Published snapshot entries now include the watches context
units.reason: Feeds the context that ends watches into the serving snapshot; wrong wiring would leave watches uncancelled.
focus: watches is propagated for every entry, including ones with a nil backend
